title: CFinBench: A Comprehensive Chinese Financial Benchmark for Large Language Models

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.1 Inference Details (temperature and top-p 1.0 with greedy decoding via OpenCompass; output length 64; input truncated to 2048 tokens) - for the API 'greedy' is emulated with temperature 0

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: CFinBench test split (80% of the validation+test pool; exact count to be read from the release)
task.approximation: the paper's unversioned 'gpt-4-turbo' is resolved to the 2024-04-09 snapshot by the date rule; OpenCompass greedy decoding emulated with temperature 0

items.source: yanbinwei/CFinBench-Eval (OpenCompass configs, Apache-2.0) with the data archive linked from cfinbench.github.io (Google Drive file id 1f80Od4j-N2uWDwNag0EfQoDFcoCsf3NQ)
items.config_or_split: test split, all 43 second-level categories, three question types (single-choice, multiple-choice, judgment)
items.license: code Apache-2.0; data license to be read from the archive

fields_prose.input: question text, options (A-D or A-E), second-level category name (subject slot)
fields_prose.label: answer (letter(s) or 正确/错误)

placeholders.prompt_by_type: one of three templates selected by question type (not expressible)
placeholders.subject: items.subject
placeholders.question: items.question

prompt.source_location: Appendix C, Figure 5 (zero-shot answer-only prompts; Chinese text present in the extraction)
prompt.verbatim: full (Chinese templates copied; the subject name and question body become placeholders; English translations omitted)

placeholders_prose.subject: second-level category name in Chinese (e.g. 金融学, 税务师, 银行业法)
placeholders_prose.question: question stem
placeholders_prose.options: options on one line as printed: 'A、... B、... C、... D、...'

output.postprocess: single: first predicted option only (Sec. 4.1); multiple: any option outside the gold set = wrong, otherwise partial credit = predicted/gold count; judgment: exact match
output.parse_prose: regex after '答案' : single-choice -> first letter A-E; multiple-choice -> all letters A-E; judgment -> '正确' or '错误'

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: final = 0.4 x acc(single-choice) + 0.4 x acc(multiple-choice, partial credit) + 0.2 x acc(judgment), averaged over the four first-level categories (Subject, Qualification, Practice, Law) as in Table 2

cost.cap20_estimate: At gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 prices ($10 in / $30 out per 1M) and the runner's estimator (chars/4 input, 64-token output guess for a regex parse) one ~230-character Chinese prompt costs ~$0.0026, so a $20 cap covers ~7,500 items; with real tokenisation (~1 token per Chinese character, ~8 output tokens) ~$0.0022 per call, i.e. ~9,000 items. That is ~10% of the 79k pool: enough for the headline weighted average (binomial SE ~0.5 points; each first-level category keeps >1,500 items) but only ~60 items per second-level category x type cell, so per-category comparisons would be noisy.

runner gap: three prompt templates by question type, multi-answer partial credit (OpenCompass: 2 points exact, 1 point for a strict subset, else 0) and the 0.4/0.4/0.2 category weighting are not runner facilities - needs a hook
